definitions.explanation: One of the pair of organs in the body that filters blood and produces urine. Commonly encountered in medical, health, and dietary contexts.

examples.japanese: {腎臓|じんぞう}の{機能|きのう}が{低下|ていか}している。
{塩分|えんぶん}の{取|と}りすぎは{腎臓|じんぞう}に{負担|ふたん}をかける。
examples.english: Consuming too much salt puts strain on the kidneys.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{腎臓|じんぞう}{移植|いしょく}の{手術|しゅじゅつ}を{受|う}けて{回復|かいふく}した。
examples.english: My father recovered after receiving a kidney transplant.

notes:
USAGE:
Note the homophone {人造|じんぞう} (artificial, man-made) — context usually makes the distinction clear.

In Japanese, {腎臓|じんぞう} follows the pattern of other internal organ names: {心臓|しんぞう} (heart), {肝臓|かんぞう} (liver), {脾臓|ひぞう} (spleen). The {臓|ぞう} character means "internal organ."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {腎臓|じんぞう}{移植|いしょく}: kidney transplant
- {腎臓|じんぞう}{結石|けっせき}: kidney stone
- {腎臓|じんぞう}{病|びょう}: kidney disease
- {人工|じんこう}{透析|とうせき}: dialysis (for kidney failure)
- {腎臓|じんぞう}に{負担|ふたん}をかける: to strain the kidneys
